review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–145, and judged it from the text alone. I did not open other sources. The only repeated reasoning is the one-line step `by simpa [hp.isSelfAdjoint.star_eq, hq.isSelfAdjoint.star_eq] using congr(star $h)`. It appears in `add` (turning p*q=0 into q*p=0), in `sub_of_mul_eq_left` (turning p*q=p into q*p=p), and in `sub_of_mul_eq_right` (the reverse direction). `sub_iff_mul_eq_right` uses a similar `simp [star_mul, ...]` step. Each use is a short calculation that applies `star` to a hypothesis and simplifies with the self-adjointness equalities. Pulling it into a helper such as "for star projections, p*q = r ↔ q*p = r" would save very little. That is the short-calculation and thin-wrapper case the rubric excludes. `sub_of_mul_eq_right` already reuses `sub_of_mul_eq_left`, and `sub_iff_mul_eq_right` already reuses `sub_iff_mul_eq_left`. The other proofs are one-line applications of existing `IsIdempotentElem` and `IsSelfAdjoint` lemmas. I found nothing to report under this rubric.
